entries.statement: A series whose ONLY anchors are source 'mu' is unverified BY DEFINITION (5 of the first 10 solo MU pins checked were wrong); verification exit = research rewrites the pin as source 'manual' with citations.

Every ruling in lib/resolve is verified OUTCOME-side (community caps: no rows/totals above cap; SOURCE_NUMBERING_SHIFTS: no two adjacent rows share a non-empty title and the run is contiguous 1..max; CONTINUA_SUPPRESSED: zero afg-continua anchors; EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES: stored type equals the override; AFG '* Filler' marker never in a stored title) so a writer that forgets the shared gate surfaces as data.
entries.alias: no one-offs — ways to ensure integrity

entries.statement: Filler / anime-only rows never take anchors — writer-side D1 gate in applyMuFrontier, outcome-side anchor_on_noncanon_row for ANY source; a hit is triage (junk anchor → delete with honest terminal on last canon/mixed ep, or wrong row type), never auto-delete; rearranged_zone_unanchored skips such rows because the rules forbid the record it would ask for.
entries.notes: MHA ep 104 is the founding case.

entries.statement: Rearranged-zone gap (the GTO 20/21 lesson): an episode annotated rearranged/graft WITH chapter data but NO anchor sits where interpolation paints a plausible-but-wrong value — every hit is a research/promotion target; zone-level-only knowledge (note contains 'zone-acknowledged') is an acknowledged-approximate review item, not an open target; loose series and series with <2 anchors are exempt.

Anchor sanity outcome checks: non-monotonic sequences are real reorder or junk (ask Sean) unless ruled by rearranged/graft annotations; START below prev END−1 is a poisoned start unless ruled; chapter > manga space+10 is junk by definition; chapter/START above the same-edition DISPLAY total (or CONTINUE above total+1) is count-space poison in a number-space instrument; a DERIVED fractional-chapter anchor is a bonus-chapter mis-scrape (research/wiki fractionals are legal); loose series are exempt from monotonicity.
bundle_parts: beyond display total (same-edition band; continue ≤ total+1)
derived fractional = mis-scrape; manual/wiki fractional legal
entries.notes: Audits home owns the class definitions; recorded here because the comments state the rules.

entries.statement: C3 outcome check: a continue point sitting below chapters the same episode already covered must carry a skip-on-arrival note (strictly greater — continue == an adapted chapter is C1 mid-chapter straddle); healed by the parity healer's C3 pass.
entries.notes: Healer named as 'apply-parity-continues.ts' — lives in research/batch15/, outside this home.

entries.statement: Anchor-density: a canon/mixed desert of >12 unanchored episodes between anchor points (filler and anime-only-canon do not count — the Black Clover 130-157 lesson) is a research-tier target; canon episodes past the last anchor render null (beyond-frontier rule refuses to extrapolate) and each is one of mis-numbered anchor / mistyped episode / real side content — never auto-fix.
bundle_parts: anime-only-canon has no manga counterpart by design
trailing canon eps render null, never auto-fix

entries.statement: Volume-boundary identity + sanity: a manga's Wikipedia boundary rows must come from a page naming THAT manga (≥0.5 title-token overlap with any series/synonym), must not run past a finished manga's known total, and no row may have end<start or a start not exceeding the previous volume's (parse artifact → heal-volume-boundaries).
entries.alias: Slime ← Cells at Work / Made in Abyss ← Claymore class; Sailor Moon v3 report

entries.statement: Structure integrity: episodes outrunning the component structure (max episode > max(total, comp end, aired)) is integrity_eps_beyond_total; a FINISHED series whose aired count exceeds its row count is integrity_total_beyond_eps (a source counts content our list lacks); an unaired component must hold a NULL span, never start>end (Tokyo Revengers' 51-50 escape); one AniList entry claimed by two series' components is integrity_double_claimed.

Asterisk review workflow: annotation kinds derive from episode_annotations (single source of truth); series.asterisk_review tracks sign-off; annotated-but-unmarked series heal to 'pending'; 'pending' rows are Sean's sign-off queue; every aired episode should carry a real title and an air date (episode-data initiative work-lists).

Manga-coverage classification: 'anchored' counts only when the frontier is FRESH (a max anchor far behind the run is stale); an MU pair adding no chapter progress is the same stale frontier; stale anchors + no MU frontier → flag for research, synthesis must NOT override (a diverged anime would claim full coverage); D1 refusals (sibling scope / scope consumed / episode type) surface as their own classes so a refused frontier never masquerades as 'no MU coverage'; a manga-sourced series with no manga link is a data hole.

latest_known_chapters is written from MU only under the same-edition band + confirmed-anchor chapter floor (release number ≥ confirmed anchors; status-string count as fallback); failures NULL-heal (a pre-guard bad write must not linger) and flag 'MU numbering diverges >20% — which is the reading edition?'.
entries.notes: Kakegurui's '9' was a volume count against ch-55 anchors.

entries.statement: MU applies to ALL series as check + validation (universal targeting); identity strictly via the MangaDex bridge (no title-guessing; unbridgeable manga flag); inline upkeep (latest_known + frontier + status cross-check) lands WITH the pull, never in a separate step.

Monotonic-start heal over stored boundary rows: keep the maximum-weight strictly-increasing subsequence of chapter_start (research rows weight 1000 and are never dropped; self-degenerate rows lose ties), re-close ONLY broken ends (degenerate, overlapping, or null-with-successor — a valid end like Tokyo Ghoul :re v3 ending at 31 before a fractional 31.5 is left alone), null a degenerate FINAL volume; when the coherent run is a minority of the table and no research rows exist, WIPE the whole table (the Ippo v61 / Urusei Yatsura principle) and flag boundary_parse_unusable; otherwise flag boundary_parse_artifact so research can restore the true starts.
bundle_parts: wholesale-garbage wipe when kept*2 < total and no research rows

entries.statement: Volume-boundary ingest: targets are manga behind ANCHORED series (explicit id list overrides); the manga's OWN title leads the page search (anime title fallback); a manga whose page family no longer qualifies loses its stale wikipedia rows; a page whose parse repeats volume numbers or runs backwards is a franchise/disambiguation page and is skipped; boundariesWithDrops drops non-increasing starts and flags; for a FINISHED manga with a known total, rows past the total are TRIMMED and the last end clamped; <2 volumes or last start > total+50 flag; research-tier later rows close the last wiki volume at their first chapter −1; wikipedia rows are full-replaced, research rows untouched.
bundle_parts: research rows close last wiki volume

entries.statement: Whole-series display verification: after ANY anchor/episode adjustment, render the series through the app's exact code path (assemble + buildEpisodeList) BEFORE reporting done; every canon/mixed row inside the mapped frontier must have a chapter (no null/NaN holes) and starts must be non-decreasing except episodes ruled by rearranged/graft annotations; loose series are skipped whole; a canon row inside a reorder crossing renders null BY RULE (no formula may bridge a reorder) and is reported as a hole (exact-record work-list), never a failure.
bundle_parts: run after any adjustment before reporting done
canon/mixed rows inside frontier must have ch
reorder crossing → null hole, not failure

entries.statement: AFG never touches episode types — the AFG backfill writes anchors only (source 'afg'), through the shared lib/anchors write path; series lookup is identity-registry FIRST, then afl_slug / own id / slugified title only for never-registered pages; 10s/host courtesy pacing; 24h resume window; --force re-fetches + re-parses after parser changes.

afg-continua anchors are derivation-tier: the sweep wipes and rebuilds them per series via the same applyContinua the refresh-afg edge runs inline (identity guard, self-consistency, chapter-space gate, precedence, boundary writes, cross-check flags); unserved pages apply at series-creation time.
entries.notes: CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (repairs on derivation-tier rows are wiped) is the consequence.

entries.statement: Conditional GETs are wrong when we hold no body: registration-tier AFG rows carried etags but no raw_html, so the first continua campaign got 304s and staged nothing — never send etag/last-modified for a page whose body is not stored.
entries.notes: Pipeline trap; the same no-conditional-header choice appears in refix.ts (parser changed, page did not).

entries.statement: AFG expansion: AFG-only shows become canonical series only on exact-match-or-flag against AniList (whitespace-insensitive full-title/synonym equality, series formats TV/TV_SHORT/ONA preferred, ASCII-folded retry for accented titles, never prefix-matching); the matched entry's SEQUEL chain is walked (ownership-guarded) before the ±2/lag alignment gate; the 60% sparse guard applies against the whole finished chain; id clashes fall back to id-year then id-anilistId; zero-episode registration-tier pages are still candidates for unserved slugs (SHY sat invisible behind the ≥6 filter).

Staging must never hold output the current parse would not produce: after any lib/afg.ts parser change every staged page's raw_html is re-parsed into raw (preserving a previously staged continua when the re-parse finds none) and content_hash updated.

Structure reconciliation: whenever a series' episode numbering outruns its component structure BY ANY AMOUNT, walk the AniList chain to the episodes' end (ownership-guarded, bridge formats included); chain confirms (±2/lag) → structure rebuilds (id/title/afl_slug preserved, scope applied, episode floor); a 1-2 episode overshoot with no chain progress just floors the totals (episode-floor invariant); larger unexplained overshoot files count_mismatch (stage reconcile-structure) — nothing guessed; EXTRAS_ADOPTED series adopt the episode count.
entries.alias: episode-floor invariant / AoT Final Chapters finding

entries.statement: Sequel-linked series sharing one manga MUST be scoped (series_scopes) — otherwise each shows the whole franchise (the Naruto bug); any such pair without a scope row flags count_mismatch 'needs scope curation'; a curated scope row dismisses that flag and syncs total/start volume+chapter into canonical.
entries.enforcement_site: scripts/ingest/scopes-apply.ts#main / lib/resolve applyScope (inline on every resolve/stitch)

entries.statement: source_map dispositions are RULINGS, not cache state: excluded (movies/OVAs, alias-corrupt pages) and duplicate slugs stay out of the AFL sweep until deliberately re-evaluated; parse-integrity failures and large staging diffs are HELD (flagged), never written.

Cleanup rulings (2026-08-22): (1) series whose AniList format is MOVIE/OVA/SPECIAL/MUSIC, and unresolved slugs matching /(movies?|films?|ovas?|oads?|oav|specials?|ovaoad)/, are excluded from v1 with a durable note 're-evaluate with the watch-order concept'; (2) duplicate AFL pages ('-0' Drupal collision slugs, flagged dups): more classified episodes wins, loser marked duplicate; (3) unclassified (zero-row) series leave canonical unless status=upcoming; (4) every canonical series gets a baseline season-1 component row.
entries.notes: The format rule mis-swept jojo/monster/x (bad MATCH, not movie pages) — fix-mismatch UNEXCLUDE reverted them and the matcher became format-aware. Step 4 (baseline component) would clobber stitched components if re-run.

entries.statement: Flag-queue hygiene: exact-duplicate OPEN flags (same series_key + kind) are dismissed keeping the oldest; a unique flag is never dismissed by a script — rulings stay human.

EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES re-apply on every episode WRITE, but a ruling entered after a row's last write leaves the stored row stale until the next refresh — the healer asserts every override over stored rows now (the eyeshield ep-74 lesson), pairing with the ruling_violation outcome check.
entries.notes: Not yet listed in the consolidate skill's healer list (apply-research-batch-8/11/12 did the same retype ad hoc).
